newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo urges rebels to resume peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo urges rebels to resume peace talks.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Thursday urged Zapatista rebels to return to the negotiating table, and also put them on notice against flouting a travel ban to attend a meeting in Mexico City.

"We are convinced that only through dialogue, only through a political solution, only through a willingness of each side to listen to the other and their legitimate proposals could we arrive at a final solution," Zedillo said during an official visit to the southern state.

On Wednesday night, the president told Mexican newspaper editors that the Zapatista National Liberation Army had not made clear whether their leaders would visit Mexico City, but added that their presence here "would be a provocation."
Organisers of an Indian Congress, to be held in Mexico City from Oct. 8-12, have said some Zapatista commanders will attend the event.
The government, for its part, warned the rebels this week not to leave Chiapas until a peace accord was signed.

Talks with the government on a peace accord were suspended on Sept. 2 after the rebels demanded an end to what they termed government persecution, a change in the official negotiators, and the freeing of Zapatista prisoners.
On Thursday, unconfirmed radio reports said rebel leader Subcommander Marcos was likely to attend the Mexico City forum, as well as Zapatista commanders Tacho and David.
Marcos released a brief statement on Wednesday replying to government warnings about his possible presence in Mexico City, saying that he was not afraid of their threats.
The rebels, who led a January 1994 peasant uprising that rocked Mexico, would need to break out of a military cordon around them in Chiapas and such a journey would be their first outside the state.

La Jornada newspaper, which has close links with rebel sources, said on Thursday that a committee of well-known left wing politicians, including former presidential candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, would escort the Zapatista leaders.

Nuria Fernandez, one of the organisers, told the daily that the group would start their journey from Chiapas on Saturday and arrive in Mexico City on Oct. 8. The Indian Congress is scheduled to wind up with a mass rally in the capital's central Zocalo square on Oct. 12.
